issues.description: Seen.ref and Seen.parent complect inheritance, clone lineage, and visited-flag into overlapping fields with unwritten precedence rules
issues.detail: Seen now carries ref (processor-set inheritance), parent (clone-chain ancestor), and uses ref=null as a 'already flattened' sentinel. Three distinct facts share two fields, with rules like `if (!result.ref) result.ref = parent` and `isParentRef = (zod.parent === ref)` living only in code comments. Either split into explicit fields (e.g. visited boolean + typed ref/parent) or write the invariant contract on the Seen interface.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as value-equality primitive in two dedup loops is the wrong data structure
issues.detail: Two near-identical passes in finalize() dedup child keys against parent def via JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b). This is key-order sensitive, undefined-dropping, lossy on NaN/Infinity, and O(n*size) per schema. Extract a named structural-equality helper for JSON Schema fragments with a stated contract and use it in both places.

issues.description: Removal of isParent guard around ctx.override silently doubles user override invocations from 6 to 12
issues.detail: Previously override was suppressed for parent nodes; now it fires on every flattenRef pass. The test simply updates the magic number with no rationale. This is a user-visible contract change for override authors. Either document the new semantics (parents are now overridable) in the changelog or restore the guard.

issues.description: flattenRef mutates the schema in place across overlapping phases whose termination depends on call ordering
issues.detail: Phase 1 merges ref properties, phase 2 deletes parent-only keys, phase 3 may overwrite $ref from a different parent. The new seen.parent recursion branch relies on the parent's own ref already being nulled to terminate. Each phase reads what the previous wrote; the termination invariant should be stated or enforced by the data, not inferred from order.

issues.description: play.ts ships as a debugging scratchpad with deep relative imports to internal source
issues.detail: play.ts was rewritten from a minimal import test into a console.log debugging session importing from ./packages/zod/src/index.js instead of the published entry. It is the author's scratchpad coupled to internal source layout. Strip or revert before merge.

issues.description: isParentRef check reaches into zodSchema._zod.parent via any-cast instead of using seen.parent
issues.detail: flattenRef already has seen.parent available but re-derives the same state by reading (zodSchema as any)._zod.parent. This crosses a module boundary with an any-cast for information the local Seen record already carries. Compare seen.parent === ref directly and express _zod.parent's type on the schema interface.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying fix — separating processor-set inheritance (ref) from clone-chain lineage (parent) — addresses a real bug, and the fileProcessor anyOf refactor is clean. But the implementation complects three concerns into Seen's two fields with unwritten precedence rules, uses JSON.stringify as a value-equality primitive in two hot dedup loops, and silently doubles ctx.override invocations by removing the isParent guard without documenting the contract change. play.ts ships as a debugging scratchpad and must be reverted. Tighten the Seen data model, extract a named structural-equality helper, and make a deliberate decision about override semantics before merge.
